candidate: maximum Hessian rank over zeros, H_0(f)
field_scope: characteristic zero; explicit witness and checker over Q

claims.statement: For every affine-linear r-by-r matrix M(x) and every x0 with det(M(x0))=0, rank Hess_x det(M(x)) at x0 is at most 2r.
For m>=2, perm_m has a rational zero where its m^2-by-m^2 Hessian has full rank m^2.
Every exact affine determinant representation of perm_m has matrix size r>=ceil(m^2/2).
The zero-Hessian-rank comparison alone cannot give a determinant-size lower bound greater than m^2/2, because H_0(perm_m)=m^2 and all affine determinant zeros have Hessian rank at most 2r.
The unrestricted Hessian-rank variant fails: Hess(det_r) at I_r has rank r^2 for r>=2.
